title: Anchor dangerous-scheme href regression (`anchor/xss`, `anchor/href-slug`)
ftml: wikidot.html expects href="#invalid-url" for javascript:/data: anchor targets (regression introduced by commit 7227cb1cd, 2026-11-04).
live_rule: Wikidot anchor blocks slugify the raw href instead of rejecting the scheme: `[[a href="javascript:alert(1)"]]` -> `javascript:alert-1`, `data:text/html;base64,AAAA` -> `data:text-html-base64-aaaa`, `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/A` -> `http:example-com-a`, `Some Page Name` -> `some-page-name`.
notes: Frozen parity reference test--anchor--xss (references-20260815-01.jsonl, source_sha256 5fc2cb1a..., raw_html_sha256 7c32bdb1...) matches the fresh capture and its binding says status=match with ftml_html_sha256 f252ad81...; the current fixture hash is 2aae557c..., so the fixture drifted after the frozen capture. docs/WikidotCompatibilityHazards.md still declares this hazard a parity requirement. Disposition decision required: either restore parity or record an explicit documented `security-boundary` disposition (today the hardening has neither a hazards-doc update nor a binding disposition).

title: Bracket-anchor reference text skips typography (`anchor/name-with-dots`)
ftml: `[#aa...bb ref]` stays literal `[#aa...bb ref]`; the anchor name attribute also stays `aa...bb`.
live_rule: Literal bracket-anchor reference text still goes through typography: `[#aa...bb ref]` -> `[#aa…bb ref]` (U+2026). The `[[# aa...bb]]` anchor name attribute keeps the three dots.
notes: Probes show the conversion in any bracket-anchor reference text and in ordinary prose, but not in the anchor name attribute value.

live_rule:
A literalized `[[bibliography]]` opener keeps the newline before it: `unterminated-0

unterminated-1
...`; a run of unclosed openers renders as one paragraph with `
` between every source line.
notes: The same shape with a following blockquote/list/heading keeps the openers literal at the start of the paragraph; only the inter-line break before each unclosed opener differs.

title: `[[eref]]` after a literal inline math falls through to link parsing (`math/eref-head-comment-seam`, `math/eref-head-segment-seam`)
ftml: Renders `[[math eq1]]x^2[[[eref eq1]` - the `[[eref …]]` block is not recognized and the surrounding brackets/`[[/math]]` become a link.
live_rule: `[[math eq1]]x^2[[/math]]` stays literal (inline math form) and the following `[[eref eq1]]` still renders an eref anchor: `` (empty label when the equation is unknown). A standalone `[[eref eq1]]` renders the same anchor.
notes: Both fixtures reduce to the same head `[[eref eq1]]` after comment/gate removal; the same shape with a real rendered equation head matches live, so only the literal-inline-math context is affected.

title: Tabview panel visibility: non-selected panels lack `style="display:none"`
ftml: All `wiki-tab` content divs are emitted without a style attribute, so non-selected tab bodies are visible without JavaScript.
live_rule: Every tab panel after the first is emitted as `<div id="wiki-tab-…" style="display:none">`; the first panel has no style.
notes: Fixtures with a single tab are unaffected. Live also emits a per-page `<script src=…tabview-min.js>` asset include and an inline YUI `new YAHOO.widget.TabView(...)` init script plus per-request `wiki-tabview-<hex>` ids; both are caller/browser-runtime and are relaxed for the audit (they are not counted as mismatches).

title: Empty `<em>` wrapper in tabview nav titles
ftml: Emits `` when the computed tab title is empty.
live_rule: Live emits `` with no `` element when the computed title is empty (title built only from a caller-owned placeholder such as `[[user]]` or from an elided `[[footnote]]`).
notes: Caller-owned title content (user lookup) is separately caller-runtime; the structural `<em>` wrapper is FTML-owned.

live_rule:
A row that ejects out of the quoted tabview leaves an empty `

notes: Minimal-difference search: removing only empty `<blockquote>` elements from the live capture makes every listed fixture match; depth-2 needs iterative removal.

title: `[[date]]` head with extra whitespace-separated tokens renders literally (`date/subname-iftags-seam-whitespace`)
ftml:
The block fails and the marker is emitted literally, with the typed space turned into ` `: `

[[date 123\u00a045]]

`.
live_rule: A `[[date]]` head with more than one whitespace-separated token still renders a date from the first token and ignores the rest: `[[date 123 45]]` and `[[date 123 45 67]]` both render `01 Jan 1970 00:02`.
notes: Found only after a saved-page capture: PagePreview evaluates the `[[iftags -zzz]]` seam false, so the preview-renderable source is the reduced `[[date 12]]` form. Saved page `muse-probe-audit2-25`, saved content sha256 041313bd96cfd4e2, two fetches stable.

title: List item opened inside a span becomes nested instead of a sibling (`iftags/list-item-inside-span-stays-nested`)
ftml:
Nests the second item under the first: `
  • A
    • B
`.
live_rule:
Both items are siblings: `
  • A
  • B
` — the span closes after `A` and the second list line is a sibling item.
notes: Found only after a saved-page capture (the `+fruit` gate is true under the corpus tags but false in PagePreview). Saved page `muse-probe-audit2-92`, saved content sha256 744b88cf6df3c4f7, two fetches stable. The gate seam is what puts `A` and `B` in one span; the list nesting ownership is the FTML-owned part.

title: Quoted tab head attribute map is title text in FTML (`tabview/iftags-seam`)
ftml: The whole head becomes the title: `label="AB"`.
live_rule: A quoted `key=value` tab head is parsed as an attribute map: `[[tab label="A"]]` renders title `untitled` (unknown key ignored) and `[[tab title="A"]]` renders title `A`; only the unquoted `[[tab label=A]]` form becomes literal title text `label=A`.
notes: Found only after a saved-page capture (the `-zzz` gate seam is false in PagePreview). Saved page `muse-probe-audit2-131`, saved content sha256 f5e712d329a1 (see audit/classifications.json for the exact full hash), two fetches stable.

title: Whitespace in an image head: live splits filename from attribute tokens (`image/subname-iftags-seam-whitespace`)
ftml: Keeps the whole space-containing value as the filename: `` (no link wrapper).
live_rule: The image filename is the first whitespace-delimited token; later tokens are attribute-like and, when any are present, live wraps the image in a link to the file and uses the resized `medium` URL: `[[image pictu re.png]]` -> ``. The same wrapper appears for `[[image a.png size="small"]]`; a head with no attributes (`[[image abc.png]]`) stays a bare ``.
notes: Found only after a saved-page capture (the `-zzz` gate seam is false in PagePreview). Saved page `muse-probe-audit2-119`, saved content sha256 a5d243b6ddd49b08, two fetches stable. The filename URL/host itself is caller-owned, but the token split and link wrapper are FTML-owned.
